channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Iran Rejects Saudi Arabia's Accusations of Involvement in Houthi Attacks, Offers Mediation
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry has dismissed Saudi Arabia's claims of Tehran's involvement in Houthi attacks. Spokesperson Ismail Baghaei stated that Iran rejects any role in Yemeni operations and emphasized that a resolution requires respecting Yemen's sovereignty, ending foreign intervention, and lifting the blockade. Iran reiterated its offer to mediate between Yemen and Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Former Head of Almaty Urban Planning Sentenced to Nine Years in Prison
item.description: The former head of Almaty's urban planning department, Almashan Akhmedzhanov, has had his sentence reduced from 11 to nine years in prison. He was found guilty of aiding fraud and abuse of power. Other officials and businessmen also received prison sentences or suspended sentences in connection with illegal land and construction permit issuance.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Electricity Production, End LPG State Monopoly, and Build More Nuclear Power Plants
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to increase electricity production to over 129 billion kWh by 2030 and build a second and third nuclear power plant. The state monopoly on liquefied gas supply will be abolished. Additionally, 17.9 km of new bus lanes will be established in Tashkent, and 140 million seedlings will be planted this autumn.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Transport Sector Sees Growth, Freight Traffic Exceeds 700 Million Tons
item.description: Kazakhstan's transport sector maintains positive dynamics, with over 700 million tons of freight transported in the first nine months, a 1% increase year-on-year, according to the National Statistics Bureau. Passenger traffic also rose by 3.4% to approximately 1.5 billion people. Significant growth in freight turnover was observed in Zhetysu, Kyzylorda, and Abai regions, with Astana leading cities.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Accelerating Reforms in Energy Sector with Investors
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held an open dialogue with investors on accelerating reforms in the fuel and energy sector and enhancing its investment attractiveness. He emphasized the importance of stable energy supply for economic development. Since the market opened to private investment ten years ago, $35 billion has been attracted, with renewables now at 31% of generation.

item.title: Uzbek President Receives US Special Representative for South and Central Asia
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with the US Special Representative for South and Central Asia. They discussed enriching future events, developing new initiatives, and implementing joint projects in priority areas. The meeting focused on strengthening bilateral cooperation and advancing shared interests in the region.

item.title: Prominent Aktobe Doctor Sentenced for Embezzling 53 Million Tenge
item.description: A well-known doctor in Aktobe, Zhanvek Narmukhamedov, has been sentenced to five years probation for embezzling over 53 million tenge from the Social Health Insurance Fund. He manipulated patient data through his clinic to fraudulently claim funds. The doctor pleaded guilty and fully compensated the state for the damages.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Discusses Bank Transfer and Cash Withdrawal Fees
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank held a roundtable on bank fees, discussing costs, competition, and consumer interests. Officials noted over 79 million bank cards and significant transaction volumes, highlighting demand for infrastructure development. Representatives from commercial banks and payment systems explained factors influencing service tariffs.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Student Sports Development and International Cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing student sports, aiming to increase youth participation in mass sports and enhance universities' global standing. The first Central Asian student sports forum served as a platform for experience exchange, strengthening regional ties, and identifying future development prospects. Memoranda of cooperation were signed between FISU and the Ministry of Education and Science.

item.title: Uzbekistan Leverages Logistics to Overcome Landlocked Geography, Creating New Economic Opportunities
item.description: Despite being landlocked, Uzbekistan is transforming its geographical limitation into a strategic advantage in international transport and logistics. Plans include developing logistics facilities on the Caspian and Black Seas and establishing alternative transport corridors. This strategy, analyzed in Berliner Zeitung, positions logistics not just as transit but as a new economic driver for the country, with initial agreements reached with Georgia.

item.title: Former KNB Officer Claims Agency Warned of January Events Due to Gas Shortages
item.description: A former KNB (National Security Committee) officer claims the agency warned the Presidential Administration about potential mass unrest in March 2021 due to liquefied gas shortages and price hikes. Ruslan Isakov's cassation appeal alleges these warnings, sent nine months before the January 2022 tragedy, were ignored, suggesting a political motive behind his prosecution.

item.title: Online Campaign "From Dream to Future" Launched to Promote Girls' Rights in Uzbekistan
item.description: An online campaign titled "From Dream to Future: Girls' Rights, Choices, and Opportunities" has been launched in Uzbekistan by the Youth Parliament and UNFPA. The initiative aims to foster dialogue on girls' rights, choices, and opportunities, and strengthen the social environment for realizing their dreams until March 8, 2027.

item.title: Norwegian Teenager Sentenced to 20 Years in UK for Plotting Contract Killing
item.description: A 19-year-old Norwegian national has been sentenced to 20 years in prison in the UK for plotting a contract killing on behalf of an Iran-linked group. He was arrested in March 2025 with a pistol, revolver, and ammunition. The target's identity remains unknown.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Court sentences owner of gas station where woman and two daughters died
item.description: A court in Aktobe, Kazakhstan, has sentenced the owner of a gas station where a woman and her two daughters died in a gas cylinder explosion. The incident occurred when the family was refilling a gas cylinder in their car. The operator, a temporary employee, reportedly overfilled the cylinder, leading to the explosion. The husband of the deceased woman has forgiven the defendant.

item.title: EU Developing Mechanism to Block Chinese Products Amid Trade Disputes
item.description: The European Union is reportedly developing a mechanism to block Chinese products from its market. This measure could be implemented by the end of the year if trade disputes with China arise, preventing Beijing's goods from entering the EU market. Further details are available via Bloomberg.

item.title: Kazakhstan Introduces Fines for Transferring Digital Signatures to Third Parties
item.description: Kazakhstan will impose fines for transferring a company director's digital signature to another person, effective July 2026 under the new Digital Code. Penalties range from 10 to 150 Monthly Calculated Index (MCI), potentially reaching up to 648,750 tenge for individuals and businesses. The code prohibits sharing private keys, even with company employees.

item.title: Uzbek President Discusses Cooperation Projects with SOCAR and BP in Oil and Gas Sector
item.description: Uzbek President discussed ongoing cooperation projects with SOCAR and British Petroleum. Emphasis was placed on advancing new projects in the oil and gas sector and establishing long-term oil and petroleum product supply and sales networks. Further details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Uzbek Official Meets Henderson Land Group Chairman to Discuss Joint Projects
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva held a meeting with the Chairman of Henderson Land Group. They discussed prospective joint projects in renewable energy, the development of infrastructure for New Tashkent, and education. The meeting focused on future collaborations in these key sectors.

item.title: Missing Child with Developmental Disabilities Found Alive in Abai Region Field
item.description: A seven-year-old boy with developmental disabilities, who went missing from his grandparents' care in the Abai Region, has been found alive. Police located the child approximately four kilometers from Urdzhar in an agricultural field. The boy had wandered off while under supervision. This incident follows similar cases of missing children in the region.

item.title: Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev Inspects Earthquake Preparedness of Civil Defense Facilities in Almaty
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev visited Almaty to inspect civil defense facilities and review seismic monitoring and public alert systems. He chaired a meeting on seismic safety, noting that about 40% of Kazakhstan is in a seismically active zone. Bozumbayev emphasized the need for modern forecasting methods and digital tools.

item.title: Uzbek Official Meets US Special Assistant to Discuss Bilateral Relations and International Summits
item.description: Komil Allamjonov, an Uzbek official, met with the US President's Special Assistant. They exchanged views on the upcoming visit of the US Secretary of State to Uzbekistan, the C5+1 meeting, and the G20 summit agenda. The meeting focused on strengthening bilateral ties and international cooperation.

item.title: Court Sentences Gas Station Owner to Four Years for Deadly Explosion Killing Mother and Two Children
item.description: The owner of a gas station in Aktobe has been sentenced to four years in prison for a fatal gas explosion that killed a mother and her two children. The incident occurred on June 19 when a cylinder exploded during refueling. State media reported the owner was found guilty of negligence.

item.title: Traffic Accident in Kunduz Claims Five Lives
item.description: A traffic accident in the Dasht-e-Abdan area of Kunduz province resulted in five deaths and three injuries. The Taliban security command in Kunduz stated the incident occurred on the Imam Sahib district's public road due to a collision between two vehicles. Carelessness was cited as the cause.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Unicameral Legislature Faces Risks and Rewards in Digital Age Reforms
item.description: Kazakhstan's new unicameral legislature, established under a July 1 constitution, aims to accelerate President Tokayev's reform program. Proponents argue a single chamber will be more efficient for legislating in the Digital Age. However, experts caution that faster processes may lead to poorly crafted laws, despite the previous bicameral system adopting over 3,500 laws in 30 years.

item.title: UN Reports Millions of Afghans Face Famine Conditions Amid Worsening Crisis
item.description: The United Nations reports that over one-third of Afghanistan's population faces severe hunger, with 3.4 million confronting famine conditions. Projections indicate conditions will worsen over winter and spring, requiring treatment for over 4 million children for malnutrition in 2027. Declining humanitarian aid is reducing coping abilities, prompting an urgent funding appeal.

item.title: Zelensky Criticizes Trump, Europe Concerned Over US-Ukraine Tensions
item.description: As Russia continues attacks on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure, President Zelensky has openly criticized US President Donald Trump. This has led to concerns in Europe about escalating tensions between Washington and Kyiv. Ukraine also launched drone attacks on Russian energy facilities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Trial: Ex-Official Accused of Orchestrating Tree Felling Scheme
item.description: In Almaty, a trial is underway for Sanjar Bokhayev, former advisor to the CEO of KazTransGas, accused of fraud, money laundering, and illegal tree felling. Prosecutors allege Bokhayev planned to secretly cut down trees in Bauma Grove and then falsely claim they were destroyed for commercial development to create a scandal.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Labor Ministry Warns Citizens About Incorrectly Registered Property for Social Benefits
item.description: Kazakhstan's First Vice-Minister of Labor, Yerbol Tuyakbayev, stated that citizens who have relatives' apartments or vehicles registered in their name, but not actually owned by them, must correct this information. Automated systems detect such discrepancies, potentially affecting social assistance eligibility. Corrections can be made at the ministry or local administrations.

item.title: Central Asia-South Asia Railway Project Discussed at Astana Meeting
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Transport announced that officials from Kazakhstan, the Taliban, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, and Iran met in Astana to discuss the development of Afghanistan's transport corridor and the Central Asia-South Asia (CASA) railway project. The project aims to connect Central Asian countries to Pakistan and the open seas via Afghanistan. Discussions covered implementation, financing, and inter-regional coordination.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Digital Family Card: Benefit Payments Adjusted Based on Changing Social Status
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor clarified that social welfare categories in the digital family card are not static. The system continuously updates data from state databases. Family composition and well-being are reviewed monthly. If a family qualifies for state support due to changes like job loss, benefits are assigned accordingly.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Conduct Large-Scale Earthquake Response Drills
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev has inspected the readiness of rescue units for emergencies. Large-scale command and staff exercises involving all forces and assets are planned for next year to test their practical response capabilities. The country is also improving its seismic monitoring systems and public warning mechanisms, as about 40% of its territory is seismically active.

item.title: Afghanistan Seeks Accelerated Completion of CASA-1000 Power Project Amidst Regional Tensions
item.description: Afghanistan is calling for the faster completion of the CASA-1000 power project. This initiative aims to increase energy production capacity within the country. The call comes amidst ongoing regional diplomatic activities and discussions on trade and investment opportunities between Afghanistan and the US.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Navoiy Region Allocates Funds for Inclusive Education for Disabled Children
item.description: The Navoiy regional council of people's deputies discussed creating better conditions for disabled students in schools. In the current year, 4.2 billion soums were allocated to equip schools with inclusive education. The region currently has 261 students with disabilities, with a focus on improving their educational environment and employment opportunities.

item.title: Norwegian Refugee Council Warns of Worsening Food Insecurity in Afghanistan, Urges Increased Aid
item.description: The Norwegian Refugee Council stated that aid to Afghanistan must be significantly increased to prevent widespread hunger, especially for women, children, and recent returnees. The Secretary General warned that one-third of the population faces hunger this winter due to rising prices, unemployment, climate change, and reduced aid. Malnutrition is also worsening.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with ACWA Company Chairman to Discuss Expanding Cooperation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev received the Chairman of ACWA Company. The meeting focused on expanding practical cooperation and accelerating priority joint projects. Further details are available on the Daryo.uz website.

item.title: Kazakh President Thanks Russian President for Assistance in Returning Turan Tiger to Kazakhstan
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted Kazakhstan's efforts in conserving rare animals at the COP17 summit. He noted significant progress in increasing the saiga population, now comprising 98% of the global population. Efforts to restore the snow leopard population are also yielding positive results, with approximately 190 individuals now present.

item.title: Prosecutor Details Charges Against Sanjar Bokeyev in Court
item.description: Prosecutors allege Sanjar Bokeyev orchestrated the theft of granite slabs and planned to release a fabricated video exposing corruption. He allegedly used political technologies since 2022 to influence people and criticize state bodies. Bokeyev aimed to create a corruption scheme exposé to gain social media attention, involving construction materials and blaming authorities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Labor Minister's Wealth Status Determined by Calculator
item.description: A wealth calculator classified Kazakhstan's Minister of Labor and Social Protection, Askarkbek Yertayev, as 'affluent' (Category B). Publicly disclosed data showed his age, salary of 1.2 million tenge monthly, two apartments, and a 2013 Toyota Camry. The calculator assessed his family's financial standing based on provided information.

item.title: Taliban envoy to Russia accuses Pakistan of regional threats and supporting ISIS
item.description: The Taliban envoy to Moscow, Gul Hassan, has accused Pakistan of being a source of threats to regional security and stability, claiming Islamabad supports anti-Taliban groups and ISIS. He alleged Pakistan arms former Afghan military and ISIS fighters in Balochistan and facilitates opium cultivation. Pakistan, in turn, accuses the Taliban of harboring Pakistani militant groups and warns of consequences if terror threats from Afghanistan persist.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Declares Opposition Movement 'Shumkar' Extremist
item.description: Kyrgyz authorities have declared the activities of the opposition movement 'Shumkar' as extremist. This designation includes detained political blogger Syrgak Kenzhebaev, environmentalist Samat Kushbek, political analyst Aidar Raev, and former Kumtor administrator Tengiz Bolturuk.
